episodes.202832: The monsoon high that was over the state the earlier in the week, moved west over western Arizona and southern California on July 10th in response to an upper level trough moving across the northern and central Rockies. This resulted in the development of severe thunderstorms across the northeast and east central plains ahead of the trough axis during the afternoon and evening hours. Additionally, a drier thunderstorm resulted in a high wind gust at a mesonet station on the White Sand Missile range. Storms weakened around sunset due to the loss of daytime heating as they continued moving south into southeast New Mexico. Another round of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a dryline across the east slopes of the central mountain chain during the afternoon hours on July 11th. Storms across the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains congealed into a line of severe storms across the northeast and east central plains during the mid evening hours bringing severe thunderstorm wind gusts of up to 77 mph at various stations across Quay County. This line of storms exited into West Texas with additional redevelopment across the east central and southeast plains during the early morning hours of July 12th.||Outflow from these late night and early morning storms pushed a backdoor front and higher surface moisture behind the front west through the gaps of the central mountain and to the Continental Divide in western New Mexico setting the stage for shower and thunderstorm activity across central New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12th. Intense severe thunderstorms across the Sandia Mountains and East Mountain communities resulted in hail up to golf ball size along with flash flooding in the Tijeras Arroyo, Arroyo de San Antonio and other low water crossings in the area due to rainfall amounts of up to 3 inches. Gusty outflow winds from storms to the north and east resulted in a 66 mph wind gust at the Albuquerque Sunport.
episodes.202849: During the afternoon and evening hours of July 11th, severe storms brought widespread severe winds to Missouri, along with a couple hail reports, and one brief, weak tornado.
episodes.202850: During the afternoon and evening hours of July 11th, storms brought severe winds to portions of Miami and Linn Counties in eastern Kansas.
episodes.202854: Numerous severe storms impacts Albany and Laramie Counties on July 11th. Large hail, accumulating hail, and heavy rains were the primary impacts.
episodes.202887: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms amidst weak flow aloft resulted in flooding and flash flooding across portions of Montgomery County, Maryland. Localized rainfall totals of two to four inches in about 90 minutes were observed in portions of the county near the Potomac River towards I-270.
episodes.202888: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms amidst weak flow aloft resulted in flooding and flash flooding across portions of northern Virginia. Localized rainfall totals of two to four inches in about 90 minutes were observed along and north of I-66 towards the Potomac River.
episodes.202895: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.203069: Showers and thunderstorms began to develop in a highly unstable and moist atmosphere during the afternoon hours of July 12, 2025. Thunderstorms largely remained sub-severe; however, low effective bulk shear values led to slow-moving thunderstorms to occur across potions of southern Pennsylvania, with rainfall rates exceeding two inches per hour across portions of Adams County.
episodes.203109: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms tracked along a stationary front over far southern WI. Significant damaging wind gusts and flooding occurred.
episodes.203148: Severe thunderstorms across northeast Colorado during the late afternoon and early evening hours. The storms ranged from Boulder County east across Weld, Morgan, and Logan Counties.
episodes.203149: A severe thunderstorm over Park County produce hail for 30 minutes with the largest storms 1.5 inches in diameter.
episodes.203169: A weak upper level trough drifted southeast into Eastern Oklahoma, North and West-Central Texas on July 12th, where it encountered a hot, humid, and very unstable air mass as temperatures climbed into the mid 90s over much of the Four State Region. While the wind shear remained weak during the day, ample instability contributed to rapid scattered shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon over portions of East Texas and Southeast Oklahoma. Some of these storms became severe during the late afternoon hours, producing damaging winds which downed trees across various areas of East Texas, before gradually weakening during the evening with the loss of heating.
episodes.203170: A weak upper level trough drifted southeast into Eastern Oklahoma, North and West-Central Texas on July 12th, where it encountered a hot, humid, and very unstable air mass as temperatures climbed into the mid 90s over much of the Four State Region. While the wind shear remained weak during the day, ample instability contributed to rapid scattered shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon over portions of East Texas and Southeast Oklahoma. Some of these storms became severe during the late afternoon hours, producing damaging winds which downed trees across various areas of East Texas, as well as large hail near Broken Bow in McCurtain County Oklahoma before gradually weakening during the evening with the loss of heating.
episodes.203354: Showers and thunderstorms developed when a low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley region.
episodes.203395: Thunderstorms produced strong winds near Conroe.
episodes.203768: A few severe thunderstorms popped up over western to north-central Maryland, and in north-central Virginia in the vicinity of a lee side pressure trough.
episodes.203769: A few severe thunderstorms popped up over western to north-central Maryland, and in north-central Virginia in the vicinity of a lee side pressure trough.
episodes.203803: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Henry County of southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down two trees with one falling on to power lines about two miles north-northwest of Sanville.
episodes.203804: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Surry and Yadkin counties of northwest North Carolina. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down a few trees.
episodes.203955: A weak and slow-moving upper trough translated across the WFO Norman Forecast Area on the 12th. A low-level airmass characterized by high humidity and modest buoyancy led to thunderstorms with heavy rainfall. Flooding occurred during the afternoon hours across the western and northern portions of the OKC Metropolitan Area. A pair of weak tornadoes were also observed across north-central Oklahoma given very low cloud bases and localized pockets of sufficient low-level instability/vorticity.
episodes.204015: Several severe thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours, producing wind damage and mostly impacting the Detroit Metro Area.
episodes.204018: Thunderstorms moving through southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts in excess of 60 knots.
episodes.204019: Thunderstorms moving through Lake St Clair and the Detroit River produced wind gusts just under 50 knots.
episodes.204024: A low pressure system moved through the northern Great Lakes region, placing the Ohio Valley inside of an expansive warm sector. In this area with humid and warm air, numerous thunderstorms developed, some of which produced damaging winds.
episodes.204044: A line of slowly weakening thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the evening of July 11th producing localized severe wind gusts.
episodes.204063: An upper trough in the region the past couple days began its exit on 7/11, but some weak shortwave energy coupled with weak surface troughing led to scattered convective development during the afternoon and evening.  MLCAPE in excess of 2500 J/kg developed by the late afternoon, though deep layer shear was under 20 kts. Steeper low level lapse rates brought high DCAPE values and thus this environment brought two severe thunderstorms, one in Lexington County and one in Orangeburg County, both causing tree damage.
episodes.204067: A weak shortwave along the apex of an upper ridge and some weak surface troughing brought isolated convection across the Midlands in SC. Instability was modest with weak organizing shear, but by the late afternoon moderate DCAPE was seen in the central Midlands as deep mixing occurred. This led to a severe thunderstorm in southern Kershaw County that caused tree damage. There was also a reported 2-alarm fire in Richland County due to a lightning strike.
episodes.204300: A severe QLCS entered northeast Missouri during the evening of July 11th. As it passed, the system produced tree damage in Marion, Ralls, and Pike counties.
episodes.204301: A severe QLCS entered west-central Illinois during the evening of July 11th. As it passed, the system produced tree damage in Adams County.
episodes.204347: Thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid airmass. Some storms produced damaging winds and heavy rain.
episodes.204543: Diurnal showers and thunderstorms yielded a briefly severe storm in Campbell County.
episodes.204550: Storms developed across eastern Colorado during the late afternoon and into the evening hours on the 11th. A single supercell led to many reports of hail up to half dollar and accumulating hail near Wray. A wind gust of 74 mph was also recorded 5 NE Vernon.
episodes.204551: A line of thunderstorms moved into Northwest Kansas during the late evening of the 11th. A four inch tree limb was reported down 2 NNW Blakeman.
episodes.204598: A dryline was located near the El Paso/Hudspeth County Line with very dry air and dew point depressions of over 60 degrees with modest moisture to the east of the dryline. Storms developed in the area and one produced a severe wind gust around Fabens.
episodes.204600: Lingering monsoonal moisture combined with an upper trough moving southeast through the region helped to trigger some stronger thunderstorms over the Sacramento Mountains with hail up to an inch in diameter falling between Cloudcroft and Mayhill.
episodes.204621: Moist southwest steering flow focused the afternoon and early evening sea breeze merger toward the I-95 corridor. Storm produced locally heavy rainfall, gusty winds and lightning. Three people were struck and injured by lighting in St. Augustine Beach FL.
episodes.204656: Isolated thunderstorms and storm clusters developed within a warm and humid air mass, beneath weak high pressure over the area. Storms formed on multiple rain-cooled outflow boundaries and pulsed up and down quickly. A gust to 62 mph was observed at Winston-Salem.
episodes.204701: A slow-moving cold front draped across northern Illinois triggered a broken line of strong thunderstorms during the evening of July 11th.  While these storms remained sub-severe, a cluster of cells well ahead of the front produced damaging wind gusts of around 60mph and minor wind damage in parts of Christian County.
episodes.204702: A cold front interacting with a seasonably hot and humid airmass triggered clusters of strong thunderstorms across east-central Illinois from the late morning through the afternoon of July 12th.  One of the cells produced wind gusts of around 60mph and minor wind damage across parts of Coles County.
episodes.204733: Stray collapse of a storm in northeast Jay county resulted in some trees being blown down. No other reports of damage received with measured and estimated winds at most 40 to 45 mph.
episodes.205183: Slow-moving thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning of the 12th, along and ahead of a cold front that was slowly pushing into the area. Locally heavy rainfall resulted in some flash flooding.
episodes.205265: Scattered showers and storms developed across central and eastern Virginia on July 12 given an unstable air mass in place. These storms were slow-moving and produced heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.205266: Scattered storms developed across central and eastern Virginia on July 12 given an unstable air mass in place. Some of these storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.205349: With high pressure over the region, a pocket of cooler air aloft allowed for large hail to develop with strong to severe thunderstorms over Southeast Florida.
episodes.205427: Thunderstorms moved across portions of far southeastern Kansas with localized severe winds producing damage.
episodes.205435: On July 11th, a line of severe thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa and produced damaging straight-line winds, tornadoes and heavy rain. Rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches fell in a few hours across the Quad Cities, on top of heavy rain from the previous night and caused major flash flooding in Davenport. A Considerable Flash Flood warning was issued at 5:26 PM followed by a Flash Flood Emergency at 6:16 PM.
episodes.205446: On July 11th, a line of severe thunderstorms moved across eastern Iowa and into northwest Illinois.  These storms produced damaging straight-line winds and very heavy rain. Rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches fell in a few hours across the Quad Cities, on top of heavy rain from the previous night and caused flash flooding in Moline and Bureau County. A Considerable Flash Flood warning was issued at 5:26 PM followed by a Flash Flood Emergency at 6:16 PM.
episodes.205545: Widely scattered storms developed in within an area of robust instability and weak shear leading to short-lived severe weather in very localized areas. With that being said, storms managed to produce up to golf ball sized hail along with up to 70 mph wind gusts across portions of south-central Kansas and the Flint Hills.
episodes.205549: A thunderstorm embedded within stratiform rainfall quickly intensified over northern Wilson County and produced 2.25-inch hail along with wind damage. The storm subsequently lost its intensity quickly as it continued eastward.
episodes.205576: A slow moving cold frontal boundary entered into the Quad State on the 12th. Showers and thunderstorms formed on the south side of the front and moved eastward through the region during the afternoon and early evening hours. Afternoon storms produced severe wind gusts from straight-line winds, while a sub-severe 55mph wind gust was also observed at Deaconess Gateway Hospital. MLCAPE was around 2000J/kg, DCAPE was 1100J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 25kts.
episodes.205577: A slow moving cold frontal boundary entered into the Quad State on the 12th. Showers and thunderstorms formed on the south side of the front and moved eastward through the region during the afternoon and early evening hours. Mid-afternoon storms blew over an awning at a shopping center in Owensboro, while late afternoon storms produced a line of straight-line wind damage in Ballard County. MLCAPE was around 2000J/kg, DCAPE was 1000J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 20kts.
episodes.205578: A slow moving cold frontal boundary entered into the Quad State on the 12th. Showers and thunderstorms formed on the south side of the front and moved eastward through the region during the afternoon and early evening hours. Afternoon storms produced tree damage on the north side of Cape Girardeau. MLCAPE was around 2000J/kg, DCAPE was 900J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 20kts.
episodes.205905: Strong thunderstorms developed over Lake Erie as a shortwave trough crossed the area. Strong winds, as high as 47 knots were recorded near Dunkirk, but the storms weakened as they tracked onshore.
episodes.205945: A warm and unstable environment south of a warm front supported the development of scattered thunderstorms over northeastern Pennsylvania. Torrential rainfall contributed to localized flooding of small streams, creeks and area roads.
episodes.205984: A large expansive of high pressure in place with triple digit heat. Extreme fire behavior on the Deer Creek Fire resulted in pyrocumulus to develop over the fire with conditions leading to the development of a fire-induced tornado. This fire-induced tornado occurred at the Deer Creek Fire near La Sal, Utah on July 12th in the early afternoon. The tornado was rated an EF2 with a path of 100 yards wide and winds estimated at 122 mph, lasting approximately 12 minutes. Storm surveys indicated extensive roof damage to a home and several outbuildings were also damaged.
episodes.206034: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts while other produced dangerous lightning.
episodes.206042: Isolated storms affected the combined Panhandles during the evening of July 11th, some of which resulted in large hail in the eastern Texas Panhandle. Additionally, a large squall line pushed through the combined Panhandles during the overnight hours of July 11th into the 12th. This complex of storms brought damaging winds to the region along with an instance of quarter size hail.
episodes.206128: Numerous clusters of thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina in the afternoon hours. These storms progressed to the east and impacted the coast and Atlantic coastal waters with strong wind gusts into the early evening.
episodes.206161: An eastward moving cold front resulted in a broken line of thunderstorms impacting portions of northwest Iowa during the evening of July 11. With only 1,500 J/kg of instability and weak shear, the severe thunderstorm risk was minimal, but the strongest cluster of thunderstorms produced isolated wind gusts up to 59 mph.
episodes.206193: Slow-moving thunderstorms on July 12, 2025, produced flash flooding across portions of New Orleans. Water was reported flowing over the curb at Bienville and Royal Streets in the French Quarter, while flooding was also observed at Calliope and Camp Street. Broadcast media showed video of water covering part of Rampart Street and approaching the entrance of a building.
episodes.206216: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed along the southeast South Carolina coast as the afternoon sea breeze started to move inland. One large thunderstorm impacted Beaufort County with gusty winds.
episodes.206217: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed along the southeast South Carolina coast as the afternoon sea breeze started to move inland. One large thunderstorm impacted the  Beaufort County coast with gusty winds.
episodes.206309: Messy westerly to northwesterly flow was in place over the area, which allowed for widespread storms to develop, some of which became strong to severe.
episodes.206327: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts in Volusia and Martin Counties.
episodes.206442: A hot and moist airmass was firmly in place across Southern New Hampshire on July 12th.  Overall instability was limited but terrain driven thunderstorms did develop around Mount Monadnock and trained over this region.  Localized road damage due flash flooding was reported.

A brief/weak tornado developed just west of  Strasburg at 821 pm CDT on July 11 with  minor tree damage observed near State Route 58. The tornado moved into the village of  Strasburg, damaging several trees from the  southwest to northeast side of town, where at least a dozen trees were noticeably snapped just south of a corn field just east of town. The last sign of damage was observed on Struzick Road just northeast of Strasburg, where several small tree limbs were downed on a north-south stretch of the road south of 191st Street.  Minor damage was also observed near Route 58 on the southeast side of town, but the sporadic nature of the damage and the consistent east direction of minor property, tree, and street sign damage suggest this may have been straight line winds immediately to the south of the tornado. The tornado appears to have lasted approximately two minutes, with a path length less than a mile and a maximum width around 200 yards (though mostly much narrower than this). Max winds were around 70 mph.

Two trees blew down near Thornhill.

Several roads were impassable/closed due to flooding. This included Broadway between 9th and 11th Streets and Kelly Avenue between 15th and 33rd Streets. At least three vehicles were stranded in floodwaters near the intersection of Kelly Avenue and Centennial Avenue. The event time is approximate.

Several roads were either impassable or had reports of stalled vehicles due to flooding. The most significant flooding was reported near the intersections of Covell Road/Air Depot Boulevard and Midwest Boulevard/Sorghum Mill Road. The event time is approximate.
Interstate 84 Eastbound was shutdown due to flooding with multiple cars stuck in the water.
Large tree branches were downed in the Choctaw Lake area.
Water was flooding Creamery road.
The public reported flooding along Tidewater Drive near Cromwell Drive and on Norview Avenue via waze.
Around Kentsdale Drive and Bradley Boulevard, a car got stuck in moving water which was around 6 inches deep. Occupants safely got out.
Multiple vehicles driving into flooded roadway with at least 6 inches of water running along it. Occurred at River Road.
Roadway flooding, including vehicles stalled in floodwaters, occurred near the intersection of Mustang Road and Southwest 15th Street. The event time is approximate.

events.narrative: The Weatherflow site in Calibogue Sound measured a peak wind gust of 42 knots.
A tree blew down into the roadway on Kettle Pond Lane near VA-7 Leesburg Pike.
The intersection of Route 191 and Route 196 was washed out.
WTOP reporter noted 1.5 to 3 feet of standing water underneath the 267 Toll Road at Hunter Mill Road.
Trained spotter reports water flowing over the curb on the corner of Bienville and Royal Streets in the French Quarter.
The hail lasted 30 minutes.
Calliope and Camp Street flooded according to Streetwise NOLA.
There were reports of ten or more homes damaged from downed trees, with 20 to 30 people displaced.
A large tree was downed onto a transformer.
The automated weather station at the Winston Salem airport measured a 62 mph wind gust.
A 9 foot rise from 228 feet to 237 feet in 1 hour was observed between 425 and 525 PM at the stream gauge Hunter Mill Estates Regional Pond.
Several large healthy trees had medium sized branches torn off and downed.
Roadway flooding, with an estimated six to eight inches of running water, occurred along Reno Avenue between Cemetery Road and Czech Hall Road. The event time is approximate.

Reports of 6 inches of flowing water across Browns Mill Road where Difficult Run River runs.
Water from Lick Branch flowing across Catharpin Road between Catharpin Way and Executive Drive.

Very heavy rain occurred with 2 to 3 estimated to have fallen in around 1 hour.  Excessive run-off caused culverts to become overwhelmed with road damage and flooding being reported at Stoddard Rd, Depot Rd, and Rt. 123 in Hancock.

Broadcast media reports flash flooding on Rampart Street. Video shows water covering  part of the road and water was approaching the entrance to a building.
